tagline.text: A free-entry white-sand beach on the Coron island-hopping circuit

location.label: Location
location.text: Calamian Islands near Coron, Palawan; reached by boat from Coron town

duration.label: Time needed
duration.text: 1–2 hours (one stop on an island-hopping tour)

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱1,500–2,300 (joiner tour fee plus environmental fee, per person)

children.text: CYC Beach is a white-sand beach in the Calamian Islands, about a 15-minute boat ride from Coron town, and is reported to charge no entrance fee in a place where many beaches do. Most visitors stop here during an island-hopping tour, and the shallow, calm water is good for swimming and snorkeling.

CYC Beach is a small beach among the Calamian Islands off the coast of Coron in northern Palawan. The name CYC is said to stand for Coron Youth Club. White sand, clear shallow water, mangroves and rocky shoreline come together here, and the lukewarm, shallow water is described as fine for children. It lacks the dramatic scenery of Coron's headline sights such as Kayangan Lake or Twin Lagoon, but it is a relaxed stop for lunch and a dip in the sea.

The thing guides mention most often is the entrance fee. Many of Coron's lakes and beaches charge admission, yet several travel guides say CYC Beach is free, and Wikivoyage calls it nearly the only free beach in the area. Much of that information dates from 2016 to 2019, so when you book a tour, check whether the entrance fee is still zero. Free does not mean costless: because you need a boat to get here, you still have to budget for a tour or boat charter, a guide fee and the environmental fee.

Few people travel just for CYC Beach; most visit it as part of an island-hopping tour that leaves from Coron town. Tour routes vary by operator, but they are often combined with Kayangan Lake, Twin Lagoon, Barracuda Lake, Malcapuya, Banana and Bulog Dos islands, and the Siete Pecados coral gardens. CYC Beach is commonly the stop for lunch or a rest.

Coron is a popular Palawan destination with frequent flights from Manila, and it is also a favorite of divers and island hoppers. This guide explains how to fit CYC Beach into a Coron itinerary, what it costs and what to watch out for. Prices and rules change every year, so treat the numbers as rough ranges and check the latest notices when you book.

blocks.title: A beach with no entrance fee

children.text: Several guides describe CYC Beach as a beach with no entrance fee. Many other Coron stops charge admission, so this is a clear advantage for budget travelers. However, the information relies heavily on older sources, so confirm it with the tour you book.

The water is lukewarm and shallow, easy for swimming and reportedly fine for families with children. It is an inner sea sheltered by islands rather than open water with big waves, so it is relatively safe, but depth changes with the tide, so bring a life jacket.

Snorkels and fins can be rented, or you can bring your own. Small fish are said to be visible close to shore, though visibility depends on weather and waves. Many opinions hold that real coral viewing is better at stops such as Siete Pecados, which are often on the same tour.
Mangroves and rocks line the edge of the beach and contrast with the white sand. It is a good place for photos on a clear day; watch out for slippery and sharp rock surfaces when walking.
Tours usually include lunch, and on many itineraries the meal in the shade happens at CYC Beach. If you want a longer rest on the beach, ask how long each stop lasts when you book.

blocks.title: Part of the Kayangan and Twin Lagoon circuit

children.text: CYC Beach itself is a simple beach, but it is often combined on the same day with Coron highlights such as Kayangan Lake, Twin Lagoon and Barracuda Lake. When choosing a day tour, check the itinerary to see whether CYC Beach is included.

items.title: A day of island hopping from Coron
items.subtitle: An itinerary that uses CYC Beach as the lunch stop

children.text: Board the tour boat at the Coron town pier or in front of your lodging. On a joiner tour several groups share one boat, and the departure time and meeting point follow the operator you booked.
Visit the first stop, such as Kayangan Lake or Twin Lagoon. Such places often charge a separate entrance fee, so check whether it is included in the tour price.
Move on to the next stop for snorkeling. Some routes include Barracuda Lake or a coral garden.
Land at CYC Beach for lunch and a rest. Swim in the shallow water or stroll along the beach.
Visit the remaining stops and return to Coron town in the late afternoon. The sun is strong on the boat, so bring a hat and sunscreen.
The order of stops and the time at each depend on weather, tide and operator. The times above are an example of the flow.

items.title: Easygoing by private boat
items.subtitle: An itinerary where you choose the stops and timing

children.text: Charter a boat through a group such as the Calamian Tourist Boat Association. The more people, the lower the cost per person.
Stop at CYC Beach first, at a quiet time, to take photos and swim. It is much calmer before group tours arrive.
Visit the other stops, such as Kayangan Lake, in order, and eat lunch on the boat or at another beach.
Return to town when the plan is finished.

A private boat lets you adjust the order of stops, which helps you avoid the times when group tours crowd in. Budget separately for entrance fees, guide fees and meals that are not included in the price.

Cebu Pacific and Philippine Airlines are said to fly nonstop from Manila Ninoy Aquino International Airport (MNL) to Francisco B. Reyes Airport (Busuanga Airport, USU), the gateway to Coron. Flights from Clark are also reported, so check airline announcements for seasonal routes.

You can take a tricycle from Coron town to the pier. Depending on where you stay, you may be able to walk.
Some tour operators pick you up in front of your lodging, so ask about pickup when you book.
The dry season,
November–May
, is the easiest time for hopping, with calm seas and good sun.
December–March
is said to be cooler with many clear days. If your goal is to relax on the beach, clear days naturally make the experience better.
In the rainy season,
June–October
, rain and wind can keep boats in port, and tours may be canceled when a typhoon passes. Leave some slack in your plans and check the refund policy in advance.

CYC Beach tends to be crowded around lunchtime when tour boats arrive. Going early by private boat lets you enjoy it quietly. Depth and the amount of sand change with the tide, so if swimming matters to you, ask your guide about the tide.

Coron has guesthouses and mid-range hotels clustered around the town, and lodgings on the islands such as Club Paradise Resort, Bluewave Hotel, Sunz En Coron Resort and Sangat Island Dive Resort are reported. If you plan to take many tours, a hotel near the pier in town is convenient. Rooms fill up early in peak season, so book ahead.

Lunch is included on many hopping tours, and tour lunches are typically Filipino fare such as grilled fish, pork, rice and fruit. Bring snacks and drinking water, and since there may be no shops on the beach, prepare what you need on the boat in advance. In the evening many travelers eat seafood at restaurants in town.
When you book a tour, get in writing whether CYC Beach is on the itinerary, how long each stop lasts, and whether entrance and environmental fees are included.
Bring a dry bag or waterproof case. Water splashes on the boat and electronics get wet easily when you go into the water.
Carry plenty of cash. ATMs in Coron are reported to be scarce or to have long lines.
Snorkels and fins can be rented, but your own are more hygienic and fit better.
Use reef-friendlier sunscreen, and cover up with a hat and rash guard.
Bring your trash back with you.
If you want to avoid the crowds around midday, use a private boat and go early.
The no-fee information relies heavily on older sources. Check the latest tour prices, environmental fee and stop rules when you book.
Hopping tours can be canceled by weather and waves. Leave slack in your plans during typhoon season.
Rocks and coral are sharp and slippery. Wear water shoes when you enter the water.
Do not touch or step on coral and marine life. Coron's waters are protected.
Wear a life jacket on the boat. The water near the beach is shallow, but there are tides and currents.
Keep valuables in a waterproof bag; do not leave them on the beach.
Coron
, where CYC Beach lies, is Palawan's signature destination, known for Kayangan Lake, Twin Lagoon and wreck diving. Most tours depart from the town.
A lake that often appears on the same tour route, famous for clear water and limestone cliffs. A separate entrance fee may apply, so check whether it is in the tour price.
Two lagoons connected through a gap in the rock; visitors are reported to wade across at low tide. How you reach it depends on the tide.
A lake known for water temperatures that change by layer, often featured as a diving and snorkeling stop.
Many travelers combine it with
El Nido
, another popular Palawan island-hopping destination. Getting between the two takes time by boat or road, so allow plenty of days.
